facts.statement: Bisticeratops is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Bisticeratops (meaning "Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness horned face") is a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian

facts.statement: The only known species, B. froeseorum, is represented by a nearly complete skull.
facts.quote: The type and only species is B. froeseorum, known from a nearly complete skull.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NMMNH P-50000 was discovered in 1975 in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness of northwestern New Mexico.
facts.quote: The Bisticeratops holotype specimen, NMMNH P-50000, was discovered in 1975 in layers of the Kirtland Formation (Farmington Member) in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness area of San Juan Basin, northwestern New Mexico, United States

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Bisti" (the discovery location) with Greek words for "horn" and "face".
facts.quote: The generic name, "Bisticeratops", combines "Bisti", a reference to the location where the holotype was discovered, with the Greek keras (meaning "horn"), and ops (meaning "face").

facts.statement: The species name honors Edgar Froese and his son Jerome, members of the band Tangerine Dream.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Edgar Froese, the founder of the band Tangerine Dream, and his son Jerome, former member of Tangerine Dream and founder of the band Loom.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness in northwestern New Mexico.
facts.quote: found in the Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness in northwestern New Mexico, United States

facts.statement: The fossils come from the Campanian-age Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: from outcrops of the Campanian age Kirtland Formation

facts.statement: The animal lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Bisticeratops belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
Bisticeratops is classified within the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
